content:
I would like to propose the idea that the explicit argument of CategoryStruct.id (𝟙) could be made implicit, while preserving the current elaboration and delaboration with 𝟙 _. The benefit of this is that when unifying this argument, Lean will use imlicit_reducible transparency.

In particular, this would be to address the following problem: there is an expression (f : X ⟶ Y') ≫ 𝟙 Y, where Y and Y' are definitionally equal in implicit transparency. Then, you want to rewrite this into f, but it fails because it needs to unify Y' with Y in reducible transparency (because Y is explicit). Note that this is the result of the fact that the unification goes left-to-right. It works correctly in the mirrored case 𝟙 X ≫ (f : X' ⟶ Y), because there the unification X =?= X' happens at implicit transparency, because X' appears in an implicit argument.

import Mathlib

open CategoryTheory

example {C : Type*} [Category* C] (X Y : C) (f : id X ⟶ id Y) (g : X ⟶ Y) : 𝟙 X ≫ f ≫ 𝟙 Y = g := by
  rw [Category.id_comp] -- succeeds
  rw [Category.comp_id] -- fails

But maybe this is not a big enough problem to need fixing.

cc @Robin Carlier

It seems a little odd to me that argument explicitness and reducibility are linked, and our solution is to add notation that makes the argument look explicit but have reducibility as though it weren't.
The problem does not look big enough that it requires such a hack.

I don’t think I ran into this particular failure (usually, rewriting by comp_id or id_comp happens inside automation, where the dsimp magic leaves expressions that are well-typed even at reducible transparency). so I agree with Joël that it’s probably not worth the effort for now.
